nodes.name: Chat System
nodes.why: Provide WhatsApp-like chat for all users

nodes.name: Chat Clients
nodes.why: Let users send and read chats

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.what: Terminates connections and routes chat traffic
nodes.why: Single edge for auth and fan-out

nodes.name: Messaging Service
nodes.what: Sends, fans out, and delivers 1:1 and group messages

flags.intent: Sends, fans out, and delivers 1:1 and group messages
flags.difference: router.ts delivers to a single msg.to via direct gateway lookup with push fallback; it performs no group fan-out, no conversation membership resolution, and no enqueue to Delivery Queue for offline buffering and retry, conflicting with at-least-once and 1:1-and-group delivery ownership.

flags.intent: Sends, fans out, and delivers 1:1 and group messages
flags.difference: fire-and-forget direct gateway delivery with drop-if-offline abandons owned real-time message flow guarantees of at-least-once and in-order delivery.

nodes.name: Delivery Queue
nodes.what: Buffers messages for offline and group fan-out

nodes.name: Message Store
nodes.what: Durable store for messages and history
notes: LSM wide-row per conversation, seq enforces in-order
partition by hash(conversation_id), RF=3 across AZs
hot p99 read <20ms via timeline cache, quorum writes
100B/day ~1.2M wps avg, 5M peak, 90d hot then S3

nodes.name: Media Store
nodes.why: Keep chat payloads out of message path

nodes.name: Timeline Index
nodes.what: Recent pages and seq cursors per conversation
nodes.why: Fast scrollback without scanning cold data

nodes.name: Cold Archive
nodes.what: Aged segments in cheap object storage
nodes.why: Keeps infinite history without hot-store cost
